kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-02.title: Tens first
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-02.body:
The tens give $40 + 50 = 90$. The two hidden digits must make up the rest: $104 - 90 = 14$. Two equal digits adding to 14 are $7 + 7$.

Check: $47 + 57 = 104$. ✓

**Answer: (D) 7**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-03.title: Count the nights
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-03.body:
Nights in July: the nights after 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30 and 31 July → 7 nights. Nights in August: after 1 and 2 August → 2 nights. She leaves on 3 August, so $7 + 2 = 9$ nights.

**Answer: (B) 9**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-03.title: Count the days
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-03.body:
From 25 July to 3 August is $6 + 3 = 9$ days later (July has 31 days: 25 → 31 is 6 days, then 3 more). Each day she moves on she has slept one night: 9 nights.

**Answer: (B) 9**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-06.title: Family by family
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-06.body:
Each family with twins has 2 boys, so at most 1 girl. The third family can have 3 girls. At most $1 + 1 + 3 = 5$ girls.

**Answer: (D) 5**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-06.title: Count the boys
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-06.body:
There are 9 children. At least 4 of them are boys (two pairs of twins). So at most $9 - 4 = 5$ girls, and 5 is possible.

**Answer: (D) 5**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-11.title: Close the gap
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-11.body:
Now the sons together are $5 + 6 + 10 = 21$, which is $33 - 21 = 12$ years less than John. Every year the sons together get 3 years older and John only 1, so the gap shrinks by 2 each year. $12 \div 2 = 6$ years.

**Answer: (B) 6**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-11.title: Check
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-11.body:
In 6 years: John is 39, the sons are 11, 12 and 16: $11 + 12 + 16 = 39$. ✓

**Answer: (B) 6**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-16.title: Build a chain
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-16.body:
Yellow > green, green > blue, blue > red. So from biggest to smallest: yellow, green, blue, red.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-16.title: Find the biggest and smallest
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-16.body:
Red is smaller than blue, and blue is smaller than green, which is smaller than yellow — so red is the smallest and yellow the biggest. Only (D) starts with yellow and ends with red with green before blue.

**Answer: (D)**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-18.title: Add all three facts
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-18.body:
- peaches + apricots = 18
- oranges + apricots = 28
- oranges + peaches = 30 (the fruits that are not apricots)

Adding them counts every fruit twice: $18 + 28 + 30 = 76$, so there are $76 \div 2 = 38$ fruits.

**Answer: (D) 38**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-18.title: Find each kind
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-18.body:
Oranges + peaches = 30 and oranges + apricots = 28, so peaches are 2 more than apricots. Peaches + apricots = 18 gives 10 peaches and 8 apricots. Then oranges $= 30 - 10 = 20$. Total $20 + 8 + 10 = 38$.

**Answer: (D) 38**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-19.title: Build the calculation
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-19.body:
December has 31 days. Three weeks are $7 \times 3 = 21$ days, so Tom was awake $31 - 7 \times 3$ days. A day has 24 hours and an hour has 60 minutes: $(31 - 7 \times 3) \times 24 \times 60$.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-19.title: Rule out
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-19.body:
(C) uses 30 days, but December has 31. (A) and (D) take away only 7 days instead of 21. (E) multiplies by 60 twice, which gives seconds, not minutes.

**Answer: (B)**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-21.title: Total price
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-21.body:
All bells together cost $1 + 2 + \dots + 10 = 55$ euro. Three packages with the same price would each cost $55 \div 3$, but 55 is not in the 3 times table ($3 \times 18 = 54$). So it is impossible.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-21.title: Pairing trick for the sum
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-21.body:
Pair 1 + 10, 2 + 9, 3 + 8, 4 + 7, 5 + 6: five pairs of 11 make 55. Since $5 + 5 = 10$ is not divisible by 3, 55 is not divisible by 3, so three equal packages are impossible.

**Answer: (E)**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-22.title: Try Ana's number
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-22.body:
Ana + Misha = 3 × Ana, and Dan eats the rest of 17.

- Ana 3: Misha 6, Dan 8 — but Dan must eat less than Misha ✗
- Ana 4: Misha 8, Dan 5 — more than 4, less than 8 ✓
- Ana 5: Misha 10, Dan 2 — less than Ana ✗

**Answer: (B) 5**

kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-22.title: Check the choices
kangaroo-ca-2013-g0304-22.body:
If Dan ate $d$ cones, Ana and Misha ate $17 - d$, which must be 3 times Ana's number. $17 - d$ must be divisible by 3: $d = 5$ (12) or $d = 8$ (9). $d = 8$ gives Ana 3, Misha 6, but Dan is not less than Misha. $d = 5$ gives Ana 4, Misha 8. ✓

**Answer: (B) 5**
